# robigo-rt's base subset: what GNU R 4.6.2 reaches of base running M1's
# scripts (docs/g3.md §14.2 M1). Generated by scripts/base-subset.sh from the
# pinned 4.6.2 tarball and oracle image; do not edit.
#
#   closure NAME FILE INPUTS   a base closure entered; FILE is the file of
#                              src/library/base/R that defines it (collation:
#                              LC_COLLATE=C ls R/*.R R/unix/*.R)
#   primitive NAME INPUTS      a primitive called, or passed to a higher-order function
#   internal NAME INPUTS       an .Internal called
#
# INPUTS names the scripts that reach it:
#   calls          benchmarks/suite/calls.R
#   fib            benchmarks/suite/fib.R
#   binarytrees    benchmarks/suite/binarytrees.R
#   capi-eval      tests/rt/capi/eval.R
#   capi-pairlist  tests/rt/capi/pairlist.R
#   capi-unwind    tests/rt/capi/unwind.R
#   capi-extptr    tests/rt/capi/extptr.R
#   pin-premature  tests/rt/capi/pin_premature.R
#   pin-extbuf     tests/rt/capi/pin_extbuf.R
#   weak-keys      tests/rt/capi/weak-keys-collections.R
#   stress         tests/rt/stress/finalizer-depths.R
#   conditions:calling-handlers tests/rt/conditions/calling-handlers.R
#   conditions:error-traceback tests/rt/conditions/error-traceback.R
#   conditions:restarts tests/rt/conditions/restarts.R
#   conditions:stop-no-call tests/rt/conditions/stop-no-call.R
#   conditions:trycatch-error tests/rt/conditions/trycatch-error.R
#   conditions:trycatch-finally tests/rt/conditions/trycatch-finally.R
#   conditions:warn-option tests/rt/conditions/warn-option.R
#   conditions:warnings tests/rt/conditions/warnings.R
#   s3:group-ops   tests/rt/s3/group-ops.R
#   s3:method-memo tests/rt/s3/method-memo.R
#   s3:nextmethod  tests/rt/s3/nextmethod.R
#   s3:print-dispatch tests/rt/s3/print-dispatch.R
#   s3:usemethod-object tests/rt/s3/usemethod-object.R
#   s3:usemethod   tests/rt/s3/usemethod.R
#
# Closures and internals are counted where they run. Primitives are counted
# per statement, so an untaken `&&`/`||` operand or an unforced argument in
# a statement that runs counts too; primitives that C code calls only by
# name (do.call("c", ...)) do not, except that a capi case counts every
# primitive its C names (install("sqrt")) or parses. Top-level printing in
# C does not count.
# 74 closures, 76 primitives, 47 internals.
